title: RemScan: A tool for monitoring the bioremediation of Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons in contaminated soil
author: Khudur, Ball

steps.title: Collect soil samples
steps.instruction: Gather a total of 105 soil samples: 84 samples from the various bioremediation treatments, 16 contaminated‑soil samples from hydrocarbon‑contaminated sites in Australia, and 5 laboratory‑spiked samples (≈100 000 mg kg⁻¹ diesel). Use simple random sampling so each sample represents its whole treatment.

steps.title: Prepare samples for analysis
steps.instruction: For each of the 105 samples, weigh about 60 g, air‑dry at room temperature for 24 h, grind large clumps with a pestle and mortar, sieve through a 2 mm sieve, and mix thoroughly until fully homogenized.

steps.title: Install RemScan on Lab station
steps.instruction: Mount the RemScan device on the steel‑scaffold Lab station, lock it with the supplied strap, ensure the station’s air‑pump and Raise‑Lower lever are connected, and verify the sample lift is positioned in the centre of the scaffold.

steps.title: Power on and calibrate RemScan
steps.instruction: Press the “START” button on the Personal Digital Assistant (PDA) to connect it to the RemScan, wait approximately 15 min for the instrument to warm up, then correct the time and date on the PDA using the digital pen. Scan the “Background cap” on the nose‑corn for about 1 min, followed by the “Reference cap”; the device is then ready for sample scanning.

steps.title: Scan soil samples
steps.instruction: Place 30–50 g of a prepared soil sample into the provided Sample Cup, mix with a spatula, and tamp with the Sample tamper until the surface is completely flat. Put the cup on the sample lift, raise it into position with the Raise‑Lower lever, press the RemScan trigger, and read the TPH concentration on the PDA after 15–20 s. Repeat the scan five times, mixing thoroughly between scans, and record each value; calculate the average of the five readings and report it as the final TPH concentration in mg kg⁻¹ dry soil.

steps.title: Submit samples for laboratory validation
steps.instruction: Send the same soil samples to Australian Laboratory Services Pty Ltd. (ALS). ALS will analyse TPH using the UPEPA 5030 and 8260 methods and quantify concentrations against alkane standards C10–C40.

steps.title: Perform statistical validation
steps.instruction: Using Prism‑GraphPad 7, scatter‑plot the RemScan TPH values against the ALS GC/MS values (n = 105). Compute the coefficient of determination (R² = 0.998) and Pearson correlation coefficient. For a subset of 20 samples, conduct an F‑test (α ≤ 0.05) to confirm no significant variance differences between the two methods.

steps.title: Record cost and time metrics
steps.instruction: Note that external laboratory analysis costs ≈AU$40 per sample, whereas RemScan analysis costs ≈AU$5 per sample. Record that the external lab requires about 5 working days for a dozen samples, while RemScan measures the same number of samples in roughly 2 h (≈10 min per sample).
